g.text: Power: the switch common is the 3.3 V rail (XIAO 3V3 pin and the LEDs). Position 1 = badge 3.3 V feeds the rail. Position 2 (OFF) and position 3 (USB / BAT) leave the badge disconnected.

g.desc: Power: the switch common is the 3.3 V rail (XIAO 3V3 pin and the LEDs). Position 1 = badge 3.3 V feeds the rail. Position 2 (OFF) and position 3 (USB / BAT) leave the badge disconnected.

g.text: Do not plug in USB with the switch on SAO while on a badge: two 3.3 V regulators would share one rail.

g.desc: Do not plug in USB with the switch on SAO while on a badge: two 3.3 V regulators would share one rail.

g.text: J2 is a LiPo connector wired to the XIAO's battery pads (two pad positions under the module: C3/S3 and C6). The XIAO charges the cell from USB-C. No coin cell on this board.

g.desc: J2 is a LiPo connector wired to the XIAO's battery pads (two pad positions under the module: C3/S3 and C6). The XIAO charges the cell from USB-C. No coin cell on this board.

g.text: D1, D2 = SK6805 side-firing RGB, both shining into the 5 mm duck hole (the maker used one 5 mm RGB LED there). D1 is first on the data line. R2: 330 ohm on SAO GPIO2 per docs/standard.md. SAO GPIO1 is not connected.

g.desc: D1, D2 = SK6805 side-firing RGB, both shining into the 5 mm duck hole (the maker used one 5 mm RGB LED there). D1 is first on the data line. R2: 330 ohm on SAO GPIO2 per docs/standard.md. SAO GPIO1 is not connected.

g.text: D3-D6 = red side-firing LEDs at the rim of the mouth (the maker's 'background' channel), each through 1.3 k from XIAO D3: about 1.2 mA each, 5 mA in all. The maker used 680 ohm.

g.desc: D3-D6 = red side-firing LEDs at the rim of the mouth (the maker's 'background' channel), each through 1.3 k from XIAO D3: about 1.2 mA each, 5 mA in all. The maker used 680 ohm.

g.text: On USB or a LiPo the XIAO powers the rail itself. In OFF the switch ties D1 to the rail so the firmware can blank the LEDs and sleep (the module itself has no off switch).

g.desc: On USB or a LiPo the XIAO powers the rail itself. In OFF the switch ties D1 to the rail so the firmware can blank the LEDs and sleep (the module itself has no off switch).

g.text: I2C: the firmware answers at 0x6C with the maker's register map. No pull-ups on the add-on (the badge has them). The maker's two address jumpers are not fitted.

g.desc: I2C: the firmware answers at 0x6C with the maker's register map. No pull-ups on the add-on (the badge has them). The maker's two address jumpers are not fitted.
